name: Left-off note check: the continuity scenarios with a third receiver that gets where the last session left off on its first prompt, and four controls where the prompt names an unfinished file but asks for something else
purpose: The continuity check (spec-continuity.json, 2026-11-11) had Snout's receivers do the next step and honor the decision in 8 of 8 directions, but about half their tokens before the first edit went to loading the memory tools and fetching the giver's record. This check asks, on the same scenarios: when the first prompt also gets the left-off note (memoryLeftOff), with the giver's ask, its uncommitted changes and its last words in it, does the receiver still do the next step and honor the decision, and does it reach its first edit for less? A free offline check (bench/leftoff-check.mjs) found the note shown with the decision in it in 8 of 8 of the earlier run's directions, within the prompt budget. The controls ask, on the same givers' work: when a prompt names a file the last session left unfinished but asks for something else (the one case where the note reaches unrelated work), does the receiver do what was asked and leave the old step alone, and what does the note cost there?
developedFrom: spec-continuity.json: the same projects, prompts, hidden tests and conditions
approval: proposed 2026-11-11: 36 Claude Code receiver sessions (8 directions and 4 controls, 3 receivers each; the givers are reused, not run again), about $1.60 expected; cap $3.50, because the spend guard reserves each session's worst case ($0.60) before a direction starts; not approved yet

arms.giver: Not run again: each direction starts from its giver in the continuity check (giversFrom; a control from the natural direction of its project, giverFrom), as that run left it: the store with the giver's record, its snapshot and git history, Claude Code's memory. That giver ran Snout as it ships with memory on, the session-start line, the memory skill and search, fetch and propose, from an empty store.
arms.on: Snout as it ships, on a copy of the giver's store: trimming, the session-start line (it names a session whose work is unfinished here when the project's state says so), the memory skill, search and fetch. Claude Code's own memory on, starting from what the giver left.
arms.leftoff: As on, plus memoryLeftOff: the first prompt gets where the last session left off (its ask up to 1,000 characters, uncommitted changes, notes or docs it changed, open to-dos, a failing test, its last words), shown only because the work is unfinished here and the prompt asks to continue it. Same snapshot, same store copy, same prompt.
arms.off: Claude Code with no Snout: its own memory on, starting from what the giver left. Same snapshot, same prompt.

conditions.natural: the giver's prompt ends as a user would when stopping for the day
conditions.save: the same prompt plus: "Before you finish, leave whatever notes we'll need to pick this up next time."
conditions.control: a natural direction's giver, then a prompt that names a file the giver left uncommitted and asks for a different small change

order: Per direction: the receivers on, leftoff and off, each from the giver's snapshot. The givers are not run again.

directions.giverPrompt: Customers are being overcharged at the exact weight limits: a 1 kg parcel is billed at the 5 kg price, and a 20 kg parcel is refused. Plan for this week: (1) fix that boundary bug in domesticQuote; (2) add international quotes as `internationalQuote(weightKg, zone, items)` in a new src/international.js. Pricing from ops: zone EU is 1500 cents for the first kilo, then 80 cents for each started 100 g; zone WORLD is 2500 cents for the first kilo, then 140 cents for each started 100 g. Two rules from ops: above 2 kg, round the weight up to the next 0.5 kg before pricing; and lithium batteries never ship internationally, so if any item has `lithium: true`, throw a RestrictedItemError (export it from the same file). Let's only do step 1 today and run the tests. I'll be back tomorrow for step 2.
directions.receiverPrompt: Pick up where we left off.
directions.expectedFact: Ops' international pricing and rules as the user gave them: EU 1500 + 80 per started 100 g, WORLD 2500 + 140; above 2 kg round up to the next 0.5 kg; lithium never ships internationally (RestrictedItemError).
directions.dryRunSay: Fixed the boundary bug: bands now include their upper limit. Step 2 (international quotes with ops' rules) is next.

directions.giverPrompt: Two things on notifications. (1) Emails to addresses with capital letters, like Ana@Example.com, are rejected by the provider, so those users get nothing. (2) Then SMS: users with `prefers: "sms"` and a phone number should get a text through src/sms.js instead of an email. Please just fix (1) today and run the tests; we'll do the SMS part next time.

directions.repoPattern: ellipsis|… as the last|exact signature|array of message ids|billing and auth

directions.giverPrompt: Invoices are off by a fraction of a cent now and then: totalCents adds up floating-point dollars, so 3 × $0.10 comes out as 30.000000000000004 cents. Fix that today so totals are exact integer cents, and run the tests. Next session we'll add volume discounts as `discountedTotalCents(order)` in a new src/discounts.js. Sales signed off on the rules: 5% off when an order has 50 to 99 units, 10% off at 100 units or more; units are counted across the whole order, not per line; gift cards (SKUs starting with GC-) never get a discount and don't count toward the units; round the discount to the nearest cent. Only the rounding fix today.
directions.receiverPrompt: Pick up where we left off.
directions.expectedFact: Sales' discount rules: 5% at 50-99 units, 10% at 100+, units over the whole order, gift cards (GC-) excluded from units and discount, discount rounded to the nearest cent.
directions.dryRunSay: Totals are now exact integer cents. Volume discounts with sales' rules are next.

scoring.success: the receiver's task checks (hidden/handoff-receiver-task.test.js) and decision checks (hidden/handoff-receiver-decision.test.js) both pass, with the project's own tests and the giver's check; reported apart as task passed and decision honored
scoring.beforeFirstEdit: from the receiver's transcript: tool calls, characters of tool results, and tokens (input, cache read, cache write and output of every call) before its first edit to a project file that is not a note (*.md, *.txt) or an agent's own folder
scoring.cost: per arm: total cost per successful handoff = (the givers' cost from the continuity run, shared by every arm + that arm's receivers' cost) / that arm's successes; every session at the higher of its transcript price and Claude Code's own. Snout's capture is local (no model call), so its cost is in the giver's session only
scoring.ownMemory: after each giver: the files in Claude Code's memory folder for the workspace and whether any states the decision; reported per direction
scoring.whole: the receivers differ in trimming as well as memory, so a difference is the effect of the whole Snout setup
scoring.gate: receivers run only if the giver solved step 1, its Snout record exists and states the decision (recordPattern); otherwise the direction is reported as stopped
scoring.leftOff: per leftoff receiver: whether Snout showed the note (recall.jsonl), its estimated tokens, and whether it is in the agent's transcript; a left-off note in another arm makes that session invalid
scoring.control: per control receiver: the asked task done (hidden/control-task.test.js, with the project's own tests and the giver's check), and the step the giver left for later not started (hidden/control-scope.test.js); with the left-off note shown or not, tokens and cost

1.gate: every receiver ran and is valid

validity: As spec-record.json, and: Claude Code's own memory is on in every arm and isolated from the operator's (--plan or --api is required live).
Each Claude Code receiver starts from the memory the giver left, not from what the other receiver wrote.
Snapshots and grading copies never hold .claude, .codex, .agents, .snout or .mcp.json.
Each receiver's workspace holds the giver's git history (a bundle of its repository) and its uncommitted changes; nothing from another direction or receiver.

A session that could pass the approved total does not start: a direction starts only if all its Claude Code sessions could reach their budget plus the overshoot within the cap, and each session is checked again before it starts.

The givers are reused from the continuity runs' folders (store, snapshot, git bundle, Claude Code's memory), copied into this run; the bundle must still hold the giver's last commit, and the giver's record, read again from the copy, must be the giver's agent's and hold the decision.

Receivers import no history at session start (receiverImport off, SNOUT_IMPORT=off), as in the continuity run, where the giver's import that day covered them: on a later day the import would read the sessions Claude Code keeps for the workspace folder in the bench's own config, earlier receivers' among them.

passCriteria.continuity: the leftoff arm succeeds (next step done and decision honored) in at least as many of the 8 directions as the on arm, and its median tokens before the first edit are no higher than the on arm's
passCriteria.controls: the leftoff arm does the asked task and leaves the step for later untouched in 4 of 4 controls
passCriteria.validity: no invalid session in any arm; the note reaches every leftoff receiver and no other
passCriteria.then: pass: propose making memoryLeftOff the default, with the docs and changelog; any drift in a control, or a success the on arm had and the leftoff arm lost: no default change, and the cause is looked at first. One run per scenario: a sign, not proof.
